Q: Why use a semantic button and label instead of a clickable styled div?
spoken: A native button supplies keyboard activation and semantic control behavior; a label gives an input an accessible name and a larger activation target. Rebuilding these behaviors with generic elements adds failure modes. Inspect focus, disabled state, validation feedback and assistive-technology output, not only the visual design.

Rebuilding these behaviors with generic elements adds failure modes. Inspect focus, disabled state, validation feedback and assistive-technology output, not only the visual design.

Engineering case: A submit div responds to mouse clicks but cannot be reached or activated by keyboard. An unlabeled field gives a screen-reader user no useful purpose.

Q: How do CSS layout, source order and responsive overflow affect usability?
spoken: Use layout rules that reflow content without changing its meaningful reading order. Flex or grid visual rearrangement does not necessarily change keyboard or assistive-technology order. Test narrow viewports, zoom, long words and unbroken generated text. A hidden horizontal overflow rule can conceal necessary content instead of making it accessible.

Q: How do JavaScript tasks, microtasks and rendering explain a frozen interface?
spoken: A long synchronous task prevents the main thread from processing input or rendering. Promise callbacks run as microtasks, which can also delay rendering when repeatedly queued. Splitting CPU work, yielding appropriately or moving suitable computation to a worker can improve responsiveness. Making a function async does not automatically move its execution off the main thread.
A:
A long synchronous task prevents the main thread from processing input or rendering. Promise callbacks run as microtasks, which can also delay rendering when repeatedly queued. Splitting CPU work, yielding appropriately or moving suitable computation to a worker can improve responsiveness. Making a function async does not automatically move its execution off the main thread.

Engineering case: A loop appends every streamed character through repeated synchronous parsing and layout reads. The network is fast but typing and scrolling freeze.

Reasoning under a changed assumption: No. A continuously replenished microtask queue can still postpone rendering. Measure long tasks and use a scheduling or worker strategy appropriate to the work.

Q: Why can React event handlers observe state from an earlier render?
spoken: A render and its handlers capture a snapshot of state. Updating state schedules a new render rather than mutating the captured value. Use functional updates when the next value depends on the previous value, and distinguish state from refs used for mutable request ownership. Do not suppress dependency warnings to preserve an obsolete closure.

Development remount checks reveal missing cleanup rather than requiring an ignore-the-second-run flag.

spoken: Bind pending updates and cache keys to the relevant caller and request generation.
